title: Eliminate DRAM-only fabs: BEOL MIM 1T1C memory in U.S. logic foundries
idea: Build standalone 1T1C memory chiplets using stacked MIM capacitors in the back-end of existing 22-28 nm U.S. logic processes, as Intel's eDRAM did, at lower density but zero new tooling.
why: Raises U.S. memory output from ~1-2% share using already-built fabs and no EUV; tens of PB per year with no new capex.

title: Training activation-stash memory: 100 ms retention, no high-k capacitor
idea: AI training stashes activations for only ~10-500 ms between forward and backward passes, an extreme user that never needs 64 ms-class retention. Build a dedicated stash DRAM with planar or shallow-trench SiO2/SiN capacitors (~0.5 fF) sized so data turnover beats worst-case retention, plus a deadline-tracking controller that refreshes only pages older than their budget.
why: Drops ZrO2/HfO2 ALD, TiN pillars and 60-75:1 fluorocarbon etch from the array (facts 1, 3), cutting capacitor-module materials and steps ~40%.

title: Substitute spatial light modulators for photomasks on non-critical layers
idea: Expose periphery, implant and pad layers with maskless DUV lithography in which MEMS tilt-mirror or LCoS modulators write the pattern through a 248/193 nm projection lens, so synthetic-quartz mask blanks and mask-shop lead times disappear for those layers.
why: DRAM uses ~60-80 masks; dropping 30-40 physical masks saves scarce synthetic quartz, ~$10-30M of mask capital per product and weeks per design spin.

title: Self-ordering anodic alumina pores form the capacitor-hole array
idea: Combine anodization's spontaneous hexagonal pore ordering with the capacitor array: deposit ~2 um Al, the one added mask imprints pore-nucleation dimples aligned to landing pads, and voltage-set anodization (~2.5 nm pitch per volt) grows straight alumina pores at >100:1 that serve as the mold.
why: Replaces the hardest multi-patterning layer and the fluorocarbon high-AR etch with a wet electrochemical step using abundant aluminum and oxalic acid; mold height set only by Al thickness, ~2x Cs.

title: Lost-wax sculptor casts capacitors in self-organised alumina pores
idea: Persona: a bronze sculptor who casts into a mould instead of carving. Anodize an aluminum film into porous anodic alumina, whose pores self-organize at 30-60 nm pitch with aspect ratios >100:1, seeded by shallow DUV-imprinted dimples aligned to the contacts. Deposit ALD TiN/dielectric/TiN inside the pores.
why: Replaces carbon/W hardmasks and long C4F8 deep-oxide etches (PFAS, tungsten, EUV) with electrochemistry on abundant aluminum. Reaches AR ~100+ to push Cs past the 5 fF wall (fact 1).

title: Closed hydrogen and tin loop for EUV light sources
idea: Worsen: flush hundreds of slm of hydrogen per EUV scanner to exhaust and let tin debris become hazardous waste. Flip: design the source vessel with a Pd-membrane and cryo-trap recycle loop that returns >90% of the H2, and a heated tin catcher that drains molten tin back to the droplet generator's feed after filtration.
why: Energy, hydrogen and tin (concentrated supply) per EUV layer: H2 purchase and abatement fall ~90% and tin is recovered rather than wasted.

title: Silicon-skull cold crucible pulls Czochralski ingots without quartz
idea: Combine induction skull melting with Czochralski pulling: a segmented water-cooled copper crucible plus RF induction holds a frozen silicon skull so the melt only touches silicon; oxygen for internal gettering is supplied by controlled O2/N2 gas doping instead of crucible dissolution.
why: Removes the Spruce Pine high-purity quartz crucible (>80% concentration) and its consumable cost from DRAM wafer supply; tunable oxygen improves wafer uniformity (trade: +20-40% melt energy).

title: Unseparated zirconium-hafnium precursors exploit lanthanide-contraction chemical twins
idea: Effect: lanthanide contraction gives Zr4+ and Hf4+ nearly identical radii and dielectric chemistry, so ZrO2 capacitor layers and HfO2 gate layers tolerate natural 1-3% cross-content. Write a SEMI/JEDEC spec for separation-free Zr(Hf) precursors made directly from zircon sand, skipping the nuclear-grade solvent-extraction plants where hafnium supply is concentrated.
why: Hafnium (~70 t/yr from a few refiners): supply opens to all zircon miners (Australia, South Africa, U.S.) and precursor cost falls.

title: Soybean transformer oil replaces fluorinated fluids in fab chillers
idea: Adapted from utility transformers, which moved to natural-ester fluids (soy-based, high flash point, biodegradable), and from avionics polyalphaolefin coolants. Use stabilized ester/PAO blends as the heat-transfer fluid in etch-chuck and tool chillers instead of perfluoropolyether (Galden) and hydrofluoroether (Novec) fluids.
why: 3M has exited PFAS fluid production and PFPEs face the EU PFAS restriction. Ester/PAO fluids remove a single-source PFAS dependency for all chillers above about -20 C.

title: Substitute anhydrous HF-alcohol vapor for dilute HF baths
idea: Etch sacrificial and native oxides with anhydrous HF plus methanol vapor at 30-50 Torr in single-wafer chambers, where adsorbed alcohol catalyzes the etch and byproducts leave as gases, replacing DHF dips and their overflow rinses.
why: DHF steps recur dozens of times in a DRAM flow; vapor etching cuts each step from ~20 L of water to near zero (>10x).

title: Silk fibroin water-developed resist for non-critical DRAM layers
idea: Silkworms spin fibroin from water and fix it by beta-sheet crystallization. Coat aqueous silk fibroin as a resist that UV or e-beam exposure crosslinks or breaks, developed in pure water, for implant masks and thick non-critical layers.
why: Removes fluorinated photoacid generators, organic solvents and TMAH developer from ~20-30% of DRAM litho layers, using a protein made from mulberry leaves.

title: Eliminate photoresist and PFAS: stamped-inhibitor area-selective deposition
idea: Microcontact-stamp a self-assembled inhibitor monolayer pattern from a reusable master onto the wafer; ALD then grows only on unstamped regions, forming hardmask lines directly with no resist, photoacid generator, developer or immersion topcoat.
why: PFAS photoacid generators and topcoats face EU restriction; removes coat/develop tracks and fluorinated chemistry from patterning.

title: Zero-helium wafer cooling with low-pressure hydrogen backside gas
idea: Ideal: etch/deposition chucks that need no helium. Closest achievable: run electrostatic-chuck backside cooling on 5-15 Torr H2 (thermal conductivity 0.18 vs 0.15 W/m-K for He) from on-site PEM electrolysis, with flow-limiting orifices and an N2-purged plenum so any leak stays below the flammability limit after exhaust dilution.
why: Helium: Qatar ~30% of supply offline since March 2026; backside cooling and purge are the dominant fab He uses. Removes ~60-80% of fab helium demand at equal heat transfer, using U.S.-made hydrogen.

title: Commodity-plastic block copolymer DSA with infiltration-grown alumina hard masks
idea: Ideal: patterns written by molecules for free. Closest: spin high-chi PS-b-P2VP that self-assembles into 16-24 nm-pitch hexagonal cylinders, use sequential infiltration synthesis (TMA/H2O) to grow AlOx inside one block as an etch-robust inorganic mask, and guide it with cheap ArF-dry or imprint patterns at 4-6x pitch.
why: 100x: removes all 5-7 EUV layers from the array (per-layer patterning cost down ~20-50x) and, stacked over many cheap tiers, supports ~$0.1/GB; trades defectivity (need ~1/cm2) and anneal time.

title: Hafnium-free antiferroelectric zirconia boosts charge near switching field
idea: TRIZ #36 Phase transitions: tune pure tetragonal ZrO2 so its field-induced transition to the polar orthorhombic phase sits just above the array voltage. The plate is biased at the edge of that transition, where steep dP/dE gives ~1.5-2x charge per area over linear ZAZ.
why: Raises Cs at the same pillar aspect ratio (fact 1) using only Zr, Al, Ti, N and O. Operating short of full switching avoids hysteresis and keeps endurance at DRAM levels.

title: CXL bridges give retired DDR4 modules a second decade
idea: Scale shift from server to rack: when servers retire after 4-5 years, keep their DDR4/DDR5 DIMMs and seat them in CXL memory-expander cards. The cards use controllers built on existing 28 nm logic lines and serve a far-memory tier at ~150-250 ns.
why: Turns hyperscaler retirements (exabytes per year) into supply with zero new wafers. Every reused bit avoids all of its fab helium, tungsten and water.

title: Tensor-lifetime-matched gain cells on 28 nm logic never refresh
idea: Time-scale matching: AI activations and KV-cache shards live microseconds to tens of milliseconds. A 2T/3T gain-cell eDRAM built on existing 28-40 nm logic lines, with ~100 us-10 ms retention, holds only short-lived data. The scheduler guarantees each read before expiry and lets dead data decay.
why: Offloads short-lived traffic from HBM/DDR using standard logic flows (no high-k capacitor, no buried W wordline) with zero refresh energy.

title: Move the 49% DRAM periphery onto idle 28 nm logic wafers
idea: Scale split by function: sense amps, decoders and I/O are built on existing 28-40 nm logic wafers and hybrid-bonded under array-only wafers from existing DRAM fabs. Each EUV-rich DRAM wafer then carries ~90% array instead of ~51%.
why: ~1.6-1.8x more bits per existing DRAM wafer start and fewer EUV passes per bit. Supply grows with zero new fabs.

title: Solar-cell silicon nitride charge layers become a dynamic trap bit
idea: PERC solar cells rely on stable fixed charge stored in silicon nitride passivation. Write that charge on purpose: a 1T cell with a 1.5-2 nm tunnel oxide under a SiN trap layer, programmed by direct tunneling (not Fowler-Nordheim) for 10-100 ns writes, retention of seconds to minutes, and low-field cycling.
why: No capacitor, no Zr/Hf high-k and no deep etch, only Si/SiO2/SiN. Refresh is ~1000x rarer than DRAM's; trap-cycling endurance is the open risk.

title: Autocatalytic electroless plating fills contacts at 80 C without WF6
idea: Effect: autocatalytic reduction. A DMAB-reduced Ni-B film nucleates directly on TiN and acts as a liner for bottom-up electroless Cu, filling high-AR contacts and buried lines void-free in aqueous baths at <90 C, replacing CVD tungsten from WF6.
why: Tungsten (China ~80%), fluorine chemistry and CVD tool cost; ~5x lower line resistivity than W at contact dimensions, with a bath far below 400 C.

title: Foundry-sand reclamation for ceria: closed-loop Mountain Pass CMP slurry
idea: Foundries scrub and recalcine used casting sand; collect ceria CMP waste from trench-isolation and dielectric polishing, hydrocyclone and acid-wash it, recalcine to set crystallite size, and top up with ceria from Mountain Pass, California.
why: Ceria abrasive is a rare-earth product mostly from China; a 70-80% reclaim loop plus a domestic mine makes CMP fully domestic and cuts slurry waste and water.

title: Silicon-on-sapphire DRAM removes substrate leakage at 125 C
idea: Minify the leakage path to zero: grow thin silicon on Kyropoulos sapphire (alumina from bauxite, pulled in molybdenum crucibles) so storage nodes have no junction to a substrate; only the channel can leak.
why: Junction leakage, which doubles every ~10 C, disappears, and the substrate needs no quartz crucible. SOS is a proven high-temperature, radiation-hard technology.

title: Fab waste heat drives membrane distillation for ultrapure water
idea: Worsen: dump abatement, chiller and compressor heat to cooling towers that evaporate millions of gallons. Flip: route 40-70 C process-cooling water through vacuum membrane distillation modules that produce the high-purity feed for the UPW plant, so heat that would evaporate water purifies it instead.
why: Water and energy together: could supply ~30-50% of UPW makeup with almost no added energy and cuts cooling-tower evaporation.

title: DRAM refurbishment line: harvest dies from retired servers into CXL pools
idea: Inverts 'working memory is made new': an automated line takes decommissioned DDR4/DDR5 DIMMs, retests every chip at speed, re-bins by retention and speed, and remounts them on CXL memory-expander cards whose controller remaps weak rows and bridges old DDR protocols to CXL.
why: Recovering even 20% of the millions of DIMMs hyperscalers retire yearly adds bits with zero wafers, helium, tungsten or water; cost per bit close to test cost.

title: Po old DRAM is an ore body: urban-mined DIMM reclamation lines
idea: Po: 'the richest DRAM mine is a landfill.' Extracted: build automated lines that strip DRAM packages from DIMMs in decommissioned servers, retest each package at speed and temperature, re-bin, and re-mount them on CXL memory-expander cards whose controller maps out weak rows.
why: Effective supply: servers retire on 4-6-year cycles with healthy DRAM; reclaimed bits add supply with zero wafer starts, helium, quartz or EUV.

title: Po fab tools are open-source: cloned 1990s equipment designs
idea: Po: 'semiconductor tools are open-source like Linux.' Extracted: fund a public library of reverse-engineered, patent-expired 1990s tool designs (i-line/KrF steppers, LPCVD furnaces, RIE, implanters) and certify U.S. machine shops to build them, so new 200 mm memory lines need not wait on a shrinking used-tool market.
why: Capital intensity and U.S. manufacturability: domestic clones could cut legacy-line capex 3-5x and remove tool scarcity as the limit on new 200 mm capacity.

title: Electroplated NiFe/Cu multilayer nanowires as cobalt-free magnetic RAM
idea: Box [NiFe/Cu/NiFe CPP-GMR pseudo-spin-valve | Si access transistor | resistive sense at ~10-15% GMR | BEOL vias as templates | Si | pulsed single-bath electrodeposition]: alternate the plating potential to stack ferromagnetic and spacer layers inside 20 nm vias and switch the soft layer by spin-transfer torque.
why: MRAM normally needs Ar-sputtered CoFeB/MgO plus Pt/Ir/Ru seeds and Co; this uses only Ni, Fe and Cu at room temperature without vacuum; magnetic endurance is unlimited, but low GMR slows sensing to ~20-30 ns.

title: PCB direct metallization replaces tungsten plugs in shallow cells
idea: PCB makers coat through-holes with a graphite colloid and then electroplate copper directly. Adapt this with a conformal CVD amorphous-carbon seed plus electroplated Co or Cu fill for cell contacts, made feasible because a capacitor-free cell has only shallow ~5:1 contacts instead of deep storage-node plugs.
why: Eliminates WF6 CVD (tungsten plus fluorine) for contacts and uses aqueous plating with abundant chemistry.

title: Polymer-copper hybrid bond whose bonding polymer becomes the underfill
idea: Combine HBM die bonding and underfill: the one added mask patterns a photo-definable BCB/polyimide around Cu pads; at bonding, Cu-Cu interdiffuses while the polymer flows and cures into a void-free underfill, eliminating SnAg microbumps and capillary underfill.
why: Removes tin and silver from HBM stacks, shrinks bond pitch ~40 to ~10 um for more TSVs, and raises stack yield against the 20-30% TSV-tax loss.

title: Cold-spray refill of eroded sputter targets on reusable backplates
idea: Worsen: scrap sputter targets when only ~30-40% of the metal has eroded. Flip: design targets with a reusable backing plate and refill the erosion groove by cold-spraying recovered Ru, Ti or W powder, then HIP and re-machine, instead of buying new targets.
why: Ru/W/Ta intensity: target material utilization rises from ~35% to >90%.

title: Radiation-detector diamond: carbon access transistors with near-zero leakage
idea: Particle-physics and implant users rely on CVD diamond because its 5.5 eV bandgap gives essentially no leakage. Build hydrogen-terminated diamond surface-channel FETs with ALD Al2O3 passivation as DRAM access devices, on polycrystalline diamond grown in a university microwave-plasma CVD reactor.
why: Carbon from methane is unlimited; diamond access devices could cut the 13 fA leakage tail (fact 3) by >1000x and end refresh. Mobility, stability and integration are high risk.

title: Tree-ring lamination: test each printed tier before stacking
idea: Trees add one growth ring per season on top of the last. Print one memory tier per foil, test each tier at speed in line, then laminate only known-good tiers (32+) with printed through-foil vias, so yield does not compound across tiers as in monolithic 3D DRAM.
why: Breaks the 26+ tier breakeven problem for 3D memory because each tier's yield is independent, using printing lines instead of a $15B fab and EUV.

title: Porous-silicon reusable seed: one CZ crystal, fifty DRAM wafers
idea: Periodic-table walk, Si (14): anodize a seed wafer into a double-layer porous Si, grow a 5-8 um epitaxial device layer, build or bond, then cleave at the weak porous layer and re-polish the seed for 20-50 reuses; the carrier can be reclaimed or upgraded-metallurgical Si because DRAM devices use only the top ~1 um.
why: Cuts electronic-grade CZ crystal (and Spruce Pine quartz crucibles, pulling energy) per wafer by ~10-30x; attacks quartz chokepoint and energy intensity.

title: Aquifer storage banks winter water for summer fab demand
idea: Time shift from daily to seasonal: inject treated surplus municipal and stormwater into a local aquifer in wet months, then recover it as UPW feed in drought months. This decouples desert fab sites (Arizona, Idaho, Texas) from peak-season shortages.
why: Secures ~5-10 million gallons per day for memory fabs. Water is a siting chokepoint for new U.S. capacity.

title: Vacuum-continuous fab where wafers never meet cleanroom air
idea: Worsen: build ever-bigger ballroom cleanrooms where huge air handlers filter air around wafers 24/7. Flip: link tools with sealed vacuum or N2 tunnels and maglev carriers so the wafer's environment is always a tool interior, letting building air drop to industrial grade.
why: Energy (cleanroom HVAC is ~30-50% of fab energy) and capital: also cuts yield loss from airborne molecular contamination.

title: Rice-husk biogenic silica reduced magnesiothermically to polysilicon feedstock
idea: Rice and horsetail plants biomineralize nanoporous, low-metal silica. Acid-leach rice-husk ash to >99.9% SiO2, reduce it with magnesium at ~650 C (recycling the MgO electrolytically) and refine it by the Siemens or FBR route, replacing carbothermic reduction of quartzite in arc furnaces.
why: Uses an agricultural waste (US rice states produce millions of tonnes of husk) as silicon feedstock, cutting metallurgical-silicon energy ~50% and avoiding concentrated quartzite and silicon-metal supply.

title: Germanium-free 3D DRAM tiers via porous-silicon sacrificial layers
idea: Rearrange the 3D DRAM superlattice: instead of Si/SiGe epitaxial stacks, grow Si with alternating boron-doping layers and selectively anodize the doped layers into porous Si as the sacrificial layers for lateral cell formation.
why: Removes germanium (China-concentrated) and SiGe epi from 3D DRAM, and enables 26+ tiers from plain silicon.

title: Cryogenic memory racks let capacitors shrink with abundant dielectrics
idea: Time-and-temperature shift: access-transistor and junction leakage falls roughly 2x for every 10 C, so a rack held at 100-120 K stretches retention from 64 ms to minutes. That slack lets the cell use a 1-2 fF capacitor with plain Al2O3/SiN at ~20:1 aspect ratio instead of ZrO2/HfO2 stacks at 60-75:1.
why: Attacks the capacitor charge wall and the Hf/Zr and fluorocarbon-etch intensity: ~3x lower AR, no high-k precursors, refresh near zero. Cooling overhead means net energy wins only for dense cold memory pools.

title: Low-pressure hydrogen backside cooling replaces helium in etch chucks
idea: At molecular scale, H2 conducts heat better than He (0.18 vs 0.15 W/m-K), so the 5-20 Torr backside gas under electrostatic chucks can be on-site electrolytic H2. Safety works at tool scale because the gap under a wafer holds only micrograms of H2, far below any flammable inventory, recirculated through a palladium-getter loop.
why: Eliminates the largest helium use in etch and deposition tools while Qatar's ~30% of supply is offline. H2 is made from water and power at the fab.

title: Vacuum-world alien clamps wafers on carbon bristles, no gas
idea: Persona: an alien from an airless world has never used gas to move heat. Coat the chuck with a vertically aligned carbon-nanotube or graphite-flake micro-bristle carpet capped with 20 nm AlN. Electrostatic clamping then presses the wafer into thousands of compliant solid contacts per mm2, which conduct ~1-5 kW/m2K with no backside gas.
why: Eliminates helium backside gas and its plumbing entirely, and removes backside-gas arcing as a failure mode.

title: Gasless chuck: solid-contact thermal coupling replaces backside gas
idea: Ideal: wafer cooling with no gas at all. Closest: an electrostatic chuck whose surface is a dense field of compliant micro-pillars capped with AlN/graphite composite; Johnsen-Rahbek clamping presses the wafer into intimate solid contact (>1000 W/m2K), and a replaceable pillar film handles wear.
why: Eliminates helium from chuck cooling plus He leak-check/recovery hardware; drives fab helium exposure for etch/CVD toward zero with roughly flat tool cost.

title: Copper-mine by-product molybdenum replaces tungsten in buried wordlines
idea: Adapted from copper miners' practice of recovering molybdenite as a by-product (Utah and Arizona porphyries). Contract US mine molybdenum into MoCl5/MoO2Cl2 ALD precursors and switch buried-wordline and bitline-contact fill from TiN/W to barrier-thin Mo.
why: Removes the China-80% tungsten chokepoint from the cell array using a US by-product metal. Mo's lower resistivity at narrow widths also cuts wordline RC ~15-25%.

title: High-chi silicon block copolymers self-assemble the capacitor honeycomb
idea: Scale jump: the chain length of a PS-b-PDMS copolymer sets a ~24 nm hexagonal lattice, so one sparse ArF guide pattern plus a minutes-long anneal writes billions of capacitor holes. The silicon-rich block becomes its own etch hardmask.
why: Removes one or two EUV layers and their fluorinated photoacid-generator resists from the array, about 5-8% of wafer cost and a share of PFAS use. Defectivity must reach <0.01/cm2.

title: CHIPS tranche paying per kilogram of rare gas designed out
idea: Box [lever: federal memory incentive | metric: kg He/Ne/Ar/Kr/Xe avoided per wafer | verification: tool-level mass-flow logging | kicker: guaranteed DoD offtake for certified rare-gas-free memory]: pay fabs per audited kilogram of rare gas eliminated and give certified flows priority procurement.
why: U.S. manufacturability and helium/neon chokepoints: turns supply risk into an investable metric that pulls NIL, H2 cooling and solid-state lasers into DRAM fabs.

title: HBM base die merged into an active interposer bridge
idea: Combine the HBM logic base die and the silicon interposer: the interposer region under each stack carries the PHY, ECC and TSV landing logic, so core dies hybrid-bond straight onto it and the separate base die and its microbump layer disappear.
why: Saves ~100 mm2 of silicon per stack (~10-15% of package silicon) and one SnAg bump layer, and removes one assembly yield loss from the HBM TSV tax.

title: Decommissioned-server DIMM harvest into CXL memory sleds
idea: Within $1M/24 months: buy a used memory tester and handler (~$250k), purchase decommissioned DDR4 RDIMMs by the ton from hyperscaler IT-asset-disposition channels, burn in and rebin them, and sell them on off-the-shelf CXL Type-3 expander cards that take DDR4.
why: Every recycled GB is supply with zero new silicon, HPQ, W or He; at ~4x contract prices a 10 TB/month line pays back in months and relieves far-memory demand.

title: Buckled silicon-carbide nanobeam holds the bit mechanically
idea: Inverts 'bits are electric charge': each cell is a doubly clamped amorphous-SiC nanobeam deposited with built-in compressive stress so it rests buckled up or down; electrostatic pull electrodes snap it over in ~1-10 ns and capacitive sensing reads its position, with nothing to leak.
why: Zero refresh and zero standby; only Si, C and N, no high-k, Hf, Ru or W; SiC fatigue resistance targets >1e15 cycles.

title: Nuclear-reject unseparated zirconium-hafnium feeds capacitor dielectrics
idea: Nuclear-grade zirconium is expensive mainly because neutron-absorbing hafnium must be stripped out, but DRAM ZrO2/Al2O3/ZrO2 dielectrics tolerate and can even benefit from Hf. Make Zr ALD precursors directly from unseparated zircon (natural ~2% Hf) and use the Hf as a tetragonal-phase stabilizer.
why: Skips the energy- and solvent-intensive Zr/Hf separation run by very few plants worldwide. Precursor cost falls maybe 30-50%, and separated Hf is freed for logic HKMG.

title: Eliminate the sacrificial bulk wafer: porous-silicon lift-off with donor reuse
idea: Grow a 10 um device-grade epi layer on a double-porous-Si release layer, bond it to a carrier wafer cast from low-grade solar silicon, split at the porous layer with a water jet, run the DRAM flow on the transferred layer, and re-polish the CZ donor for 30-50 reuses.
why: DRAM uses only the top ~5 um of a 775 um prime wafer; cuts prime polysilicon and crucible quartz per bit ~20x and lowers wafer cost.

title: Copper heap-leach playbook: bacteria mine tungsten and gallium domestically
idea: Copper mines pull metal from low-grade heaps with acidophilic bacteria; apply engineered bioleaching heaps to Nevada tungsten-skarn tailings, Appalachian coal fly ash and alumina red mud to dissolve W, Ga and Ge, then recover them by solvent extraction and ion exchange.
why: Supplies U.S. fabs with tungsten, gallium and germanium (all China-dominated and export-controlled) from existing waste piles at low capital; semiconductor demand is small in tonnage, so modest heaps suffice.

title: CD-stamping nanoimprint patterns capacitorless arrays without EUV
idea: Optical-disc plants stamped nanoscale pits from nickel masters by the billion. Adapt jet-and-flash nanoimprint with replica templates for the repetitive array layers of a capacitor-free vertical-transistor cell, where there is no landing-pad-to-capacitor overlay chain to break, and keep DUV only for periphery.
why: EUV has one supplier, draws ~1 MW per scanner and consumes tin and hydrogen. Imprint uses ~1/10 the energy and no EUV, and removing the capacitor removes the hardest overlay stack.

title: Green DPSS laser zone-melting builds single-crystal tiers for 3D DRAM
idea: Box [lateral cap | crystalline-Si transistor per tier | voltage SA | monolithic 3D tiers | deposited a-Si on SiO2 with Si seed vias | 532 nm diode-pumped laser lateral zone melt in vacuum]: melt each deposited a-Si tier in narrow scanning lines that carry crystal orientation laterally out of the seed vias, giving near-single-crystal islands with no excimer (XeCl) laser and no epi.
why: 3D DRAM needs 26+ crystalline tiers: this avoids SiGe/Ge epi superlattices and rare-gas excimer lasers, at a per-tier cost of one laser scan.

title: Nose-to-tail butcher saves the silicon ground off HBM wafers
idea: Persona: a nose-to-tail butcher who wastes nothing. HBM core dies are thinned from 775 um to ~40 um, which grinds ~95% of each prime wafer into slurry. Instead, while the wafer sits on its carrier, focus an IR laser 60 um below the devices to make a cleave plane (stealth slicing). Split off the ~700 um back slab and polish it for reuse as a test or prime wafer.
why: Recovers ~0.9 wafer-equivalent of silicon per HBM wafer. Halves the crystal growth, crucibles, polysilicon and energy behind HBM bits, and cuts grinding water and consumables.

title: Thermochromic-window vanadium dioxide as a Mott-transition latch cell
idea: Smart-window coatings switch VO2 between insulator and metal. Adapt a strain-tuned nanoscale VO2 element in series with an access transistor, using the transition's hysteresis window to hold two stable resistance states, with vanadium recovered from US steel slag and refinery residues.
why: A capacitor-free cell with a sub-ns transition, using vanadium from domestic waste streams instead of China/Russia. It trades refresh for a small hold bias.

title: Electric-arc-furnace scrap loop: wire-saw kerf remelted into wafer feedstock
idea: Steel's electric-arc-furnace route makes new steel from scrap. Recover the ~30-40% of each ingot lost as diamond-wire kerf, strip its surface oxide with HF vapor, densify it by induction melting, and purify it by directional solidification plus vacuum refining into feedstock for handle, test and dummy wafers.
why: Raises silicon yield per kg of polysilicon, crucible and argon ~1.4x for the non-device wafers that are 20-30% of fab wafer starts, freeing crystal-growth capacity and quartz for device wafers.

title: Hafnium-free antiferroelectric zirconia capacitor storing switched charge
idea: Periodic-table walk, Zr (40): use pure tetragonal ZrO2's field-induced double hysteresis loop, biasing the plate at the loop midpoint so each write swings through one antiferroelectric loop and releases ~20-30 uC/cm2 instead of ~5-8 uC/cm2 linear charge; zero-field relaxation avoids ferroelectric imprint.
why: 2-3x effective Cs at AR<=40 with Zr (~100x more abundant than Hf, whose world output is ~70-80 t/yr).

title: Copper anode slime yields selenium-tellurium p-channel access transistors
idea: Copper refineries recover selenium and tellurium from anode slimes, and Utah produces both; evaporate SexTe1-x films below 200 C as p-channel transistors for BEOL-stacked gain cells, raising the bandgap to ~1 eV with selenium to hold leakage down, paired with an n-type zinc oxide device.
why: Removes indium and gallium (China-concentrated and export-controlled) from stacked oxide-semiconductor DRAM, using a material whose whole U.S. chain already exists as a refinery byproduct.

title: Endpoint-sensed rinses replace fixed-time water rinses
idea: Within $1M/24 months: retrofit wet benches with inline resistivity and TOC sensors in the rinse drain and software that ends each rinse when effluent purity recovers, instead of fixed worst-case recipes; pilot on 10 benches.
why: Fixed-time rinses overspend UPW by ~20-40%; endpointing saves water and UPW-production energy per wafer with no process change.

title: Eliminate energy-blind memory buying: pJ-per-bit indexed offtake contracts
idea: A hyperscaler and DOE consortium guarantees 7-year premium offtake for memory measured at <=0.5 pJ per useful bit under a public JEDEC-style energy test, with CHIPS grants for converting U.S. lines to such products.
why: Makes 10x-energy designs bankable; each 10x cut trims data-center power, grid build-out and cooling water.

title: Dry cleaning revival: vapor HF and UV-ozone replace wet benches
idea: Revive 1990s anhydrous HF/alcohol vapor oxide etching and UV-ozone organic removal for a large share of the 100+ wet clean steps in a DRAM flow, keeping RCA wet cleans only where particles demand them.
why: Water and energy: DRAM fabs use millions of gallons of ultrapure water a day; claims a 30-40% cut in ultrapure water and less chemical waste.

title: Naval-reactor hafnium trap avoided: zirconia-only periphery gate stacks
idea: Hafnium exists only as a byproduct of making Hf-free zirconium for naval and power reactors, so its supply is hostage to nuclear demand. Build DRAM-periphery HKMG transistors with ALD ZrO2 or La-doped ZrO2 on a SiON interlayer (TEMAZ precursor, standard in university ALD) and characterize EOT, mobility and PBTI against HfO2.
why: Removes hafnium from DRAM periphery using zirconium, which is roughly 20-50x more available, at similar k ~25-35.

title: Apollo rope memory reborn: laser-programmed inductive ROM for frozen weights
idea: Revive Apollo core-rope ROM, where each bit is whether a sense wire threads or bypasses a shared core: on a mature-node die with ferrite micro-transformers, a laser-cut or inkjet last-metal layer sets the threading choice after fab, so one die type can store any frozen model's weights.
why: No EUV, no per-model masks, no refresh, and no DRAM bits spent on weights; uses only Fe, Ni and Cu; claims to free 50-80% of inference DRAM capacity for KV cache.

title: Waste silicon tetrachloride becomes synthetic-silica crucibles beside polysilicon plants
idea: Crucible purity is set by metal content, not geology: Siemens polysilicon plants co-produce ~10-20 kg SiCl4 per kg Si, which flame hydrolysis (SiCl4 + 2H2 + O2 -> SiO2 + 4HCl, HCl recycled) turns into ppb-metal synthetic silica grain. Arc-fuse crucibles from it with a Ba-devitrified crystalline outer shell for 1450 C creep strength.
why: Breaks the >80% Spruce Pine HPQ dependence using a US waste stream next to existing polysilicon plants; synthetic grain is ~10x purer than natural HPQ.

title: Shared energy-recovery free-electron laser feeds a whole EUV fab
idea: Tin-plasma EUV converts wall power at ~0.02%; an energy-recovery-linac FEL recycles the electron beam's energy and lases at 13.5 nm at ~0.1-1% wall-plug. One 10 kW source split by grazing-incidence optics feeds 10-20 scanners with no tin droplets and no hydrogen debris flow.
why: EUV electricity down ~5-10x and the tin-source/hydrogen chain removed, building on US national-lab accelerator expertise.

title: Po tungsten never existed: high-pressure aluminum force-fill plugs
idea: Po: 'tungsten was never discovered.' Extracted: fill all contacts and vias with PVD aluminum forced into the holes at ~700 atm and ~400 C (the mid-1990s force-fill method) over a thin Ti wetting layer, replacing CVD tungsten plugs and the WF6 precursor.
why: Tungsten chokepoint (China ~80%) and fluorine chemistry removed from interconnect; aluminum is abundant and U.S.-smelted, with lower via resistance than tungsten.

title: Forcefill revived: high-pressure aluminum extrusion replaces tungsten contact plugs
idea: Trikon's Forcefill pushed sputtered aluminum into vias with ~700 atm argon and died only because copper damascene took over logic wiring. DRAM still fills every contact and bitline plug with CVD tungsten from WF6; fill the plugs formed after the capacitor anneals with Al-Si-Cu by high-pressure extrusion over a thin TiN liner.
why: Removes tungsten (~80% China) and WF6 fluorine chemistry from back-end plugs; aluminum is abundant and smelted in North America; Al's lower resistivity in narrow plugs trims RC ~30%; argon pressure gas is plentiful.

title: Substitute one shared free-electron laser for many tin-plasma EUV sources
idea: Build an energy-recovery-linac free-electron laser producing ~10 kW of 13.5 nm light and split it by grazing-incidence mirrors to 10-20 scanners, replacing per-tool tin-droplet plasma sources from a single supplier.
why: ~3-5x lower EUV electrical power per wafer, no tin debris or collector consumables, and the scarce single-source module becomes shared infrastructure for the 5-7 EUV DRAM layers.

title: Synchrotron-style shared light source: free-electron laser feeds many scanners
idea: Cities replaced household generators with central power plants. Build one energy-recovery-linac free-electron laser per fab and split its multi-kW EUV beam to 10-20 scanners, replacing per-scanner laser-produced tin-plasma sources; wafers and DDR/HBM products are unchanged.
why: Cuts EUV wall-plug power per wafer several-fold (each tin-plasma source draws ~1 MW), adds a second EUV-source path beyond the single supplier, and higher dose reduces stochastic defects.

title: Po one lightbulb lights the whole fab: shared FEL EUV source
idea: Po: 'one lightbulb lights every scanner in the fab.' Extracted: drive 10-20 scanners from a single energy-recovery-linac free-electron laser at 13.5 nm, distributed by grazing-incidence beamlines, replacing per-scanner tin-droplet laser-produced-plasma sources.
why: EUV energy (~1 MW per LPP scanner) and tin/hydrogen consumption: several-fold lower wall-plug energy per exposed wafer and higher available dose, which permits lower-defect resists.

title: Dry-first cleaning: supercritical CO2 and atomic hydrogen replace RCA
idea: Worsen: rinse every wafer hundreds of times with single-pass ultrapure water in drought-prone regions. Flip: re-sequence the flow so particles and organics are removed with supercritical CO2 plus a recyclable co-solvent, and native oxide and metals with remote atomic-hydrogen radicals, keeping wet steps only where unavoidable.
why: Water and UPW energy: targets ~60-70% less UPW per wafer. scCO2 also dries AR 70+ capacitor pillars without stiction collapse, which raises yield.

title: Po photoresist from shrimp shells: water-developed chitosan resist
idea: Po: 'photoresist is made from seafood waste.' Extracted: use a chemically modified chitosan or cellulose resist with non-fluorinated photo-crosslinkers that develops in plain water, applied to the non-critical DRAM layers (implants, pads, periphery), which are the majority of mask steps.
why: PFAS (fluorinated PAGs and surfactants facing EU restriction) and TMAH developer removed from most litho steps; renewable feedstock; lighter wastewater load.

title: Vacuum-free tier stacks grown by pulsed-electrodeposition superlattices
idea: Ideal: a 3D memory stack poured from a bath. Closest: pulse-electroplate 100+ periods of Ni or Cu conductor layers alternating with cathodically deposited ZnO semiconductor/dielectric layers (~20-40 nm each, <90 C, aqueous) to replace CVD/PVD tier depositions for 3D gain-cell stacks.
why: 100x path: plating tools ~$1-3M vs $10-30M vacuum clusters, no helium or vacuum pumps, abundant Zn/Ni/Cu; tier cost falls ~10-30x, which with self-patterned holes targets ~$0.1/GB. Trades film quality and interface traps (more refresh).

title: Immune self-tolerance binning keeps dies with weak cells
idea: The immune system learns to tolerate self after thymic screening instead of destroying every odd cell. At wafer sort, write each die's weak-retention rows into an on-die fuse self-map and ship the die with per-row adaptive refresh and remapping, instead of scrapping dies that fail a uniform 64 ms test.
why: Raises good-die yield 5-15% at 1-beta/1-gamma nodes, so fewer wafers (and less quartz, helium and energy) go into each GB sold.

title: Barrierless copper-aluminum intermetallic local interconnect
idea: Periodic-table walk, Cu (29) with Al: use ordered intermetallics such as CuAl2, whose short electron mean free path keeps resistivity flat down to ~10 nm and which do not diffuse into dielectrics, so no TaN/Ta or Co liners; deposit by co-sputter plus 400 C anneal or subtractive Cl2 etch.
why: Removes W, Ta, Co and Ru from the tightest DRAM pitches; ~2x lower line resistance than W at 12 nm.

title: Kitchen microwave volumetric heating anneals capacitors at low thermal budget
idea: Microwave ovens heat the water in food rather than the oven walls. Use 2.45-5.8 GHz variable-frequency microwave annealing that couples selectively into doped silicon and ZrO2 dipoles to activate junctions and crystallize the tetragonal high-k phase at a substrate temperature ~150-200 C lower than RTP or furnace, with no change to the DDR/HBM die interface.
why: Preserves TiN/high-k interfaces (higher k, lower leakage) and abrupt junctions (less GIDL), cutting thermal-process energy ~50% and enabling higher Cs from existing materials.

title: Tire-retreading economics: remanufactured DDR modules from retired servers
idea: Truck fleets retread tire casings at ~30-50% of new cost. Build remanufacturing lines that pull DIMMs from decommissioned hyperscale servers, run at-speed JEDEC/MBIST screening plus row-hammer and retention re-binning, rework failed packages, and re-certify them as warranted standard DDR4/DDR5 RDIMMs for slower-tier servers.
why: Hyperscalers retire millions of DIMMs a year; recovering 20-30% adds usable supply with zero new wafers, helium or quartz, at a fraction of 4x-inflated new-module prices.

title: Rutile TiO2 capacitors templated on MoO2 instead of scarce ruthenium
idea: Rutile-TiO2 DRAM capacitors (k~80-100) died on Ru/RuO2 bottom electrodes, a South African PGM that is costly and hard to etch, plus leakage. Template rutile on MoO2, a conductive rutile-structure oxide formed by in-situ oxidation of a Mo electrode, and suppress leakage with Al doping and a sub-nm Al2O3 interlayer.
why: k~80 versus ~40 for ZrO2/Al2O3/ZrO2 hits the 'k~70' route through the charge wall, letting pillars drop from 60-75:1 to ~35:1; removes Zr/Hf and Ru; Ti, Mo, Al are abundant; ~40% less deep etch and deposition gas.

title: Planar ferrite inductors revive core memory at micron scale
idea: Power-supply makers now print MnZn/NiZn ferrite planar cores on silicon. Adapt this to bring back magnetic core memory: a 1-2 um ferrite toroid per bit, threaded by BEOL wordline, bitline and sense traces, with coincident-current writes and on-die restore-after-read.
why: Core was DRAM-class working memory before DRAM: no capacitor, no leakage, no refresh, unlimited endurance, all iron/manganese/zinc oxides. Density is the hurdle; the aim is ~10-20 F2 per tier across many stacked BEOL tiers.

title: Spider web: MOF cartridges catch and recycle fluorocarbon etch gases
idea: Stimulus 'spider web' (a net tuned to its prey) -> put metal-organic-framework adsorbent beds, pore-tuned to C4F8, C4F6, NF3 and SF6, on etch exhausts instead of burn-box abatement; temperature-swing regenerate, purify and return captured gas to cylinders.
why: Fluorocarbons are PFAS-classified, high-GWP (NF3 ~17,000) and few-supplier; 70-90% recapture cuts purchases and emissions together.

title: Microwave tunnel-diode latch makes a refresh-free one-transistor SRAM
idea: Microwave oscillators exploited the negative resistance of Esaki tunnel diodes. Adapt two series Si/SiGe interband tunnel diodes as the bistable load on a single access transistor (1T-2TD), forming a static latch at roughly 2x DRAM-cell area with no capacitor.
why: Eliminates both capacitor and refresh (Fact 3) using only Si, SiGe and dopants. It needs a room-temperature peak-to-valley ratio >3 at very low valley current.

title: Copper-oxide rectifier revival: diode-access capacitor crosspoint, stacked tiers
idea: Revive the 1920s cuprous-oxide rectifier as a BEOL p-Cu2O/n-ZnO heterojunction diode in series with a MIM capacitor at each crosspoint, selected coincident-current style like core planes (half-select stays below diode turn-on) and stacked in several DUV-patterned tiers.
why: No access transistor, no tungsten, no Hf and no EUV, using abundant Cu, Zn and O; claims 4F2 per tier over 4 tiers; the honest risk is diode reverse leakage limiting retention.

title: Po the cell latches like a light switch: implanted vertical thyristor
idea: Po: 'memory that holds itself like a light switch.' Extracted: build a p-n-p-n thyristor vertically in bulk silicon with stacked high-energy implants under a 180 nm pillar, gated by one wordline; the cell latches on or off with no capacitor or high-k and holds data with a tiny standby bias instead of refresh.
why: Removes capacitor materials (Hf, Zr, TiN) and the charge wall; a ~4F2 vertical cell lets a 180 nm line reach useful density, with refresh replaced by low hold current.

title: Metal-assisted chemical etching digs 200:1 silicon trench capacitors plasma-free
idea: Scale jump: a few-nm noble-metal catalyst mesh, patterned once, sinks into silicon in HF/H2O2 like a nanoscale drill and opens holes with AR >200:1 without fluorocarbon plasma. This revives trench-capacitor DRAM with the capacitor dug into the substrate beneath a vertical access transistor. The catalyst is stripped in iodide before any thermal step.
why: Bypasses the 60-75:1 mold etch that consumes C4F6/C4F8 PFAS-class gases. Deeper trenches give >10 fF per cell. Metal contamination of the leakage tail is the main risk.

title: CCD memory resurrected for AI weight streaming, where serial access wins
idea: Fairchild and Intel CCD memories (1970s, up to 256 kb) died because serial access gave long latency versus random-access DRAM. AI inference streams weights and KV pages sequentially, so build loops of 1k-4k charge-transfer stages per bitline that burst at GHz rates into one sense amp; cells are contactless overlapping-gate wells with no capacitor stack and no per-cell tungsten contact.
why: No per-cell W plugs (tungsten ~80% China) and no high-AR capacitor; constant circulation is the refresh; periphery shrinks to one sense amp per thousands of bits (attacks the 49% periphery share); est. 2-3x bits per wafer for streaming tiers.

title: Liquid-nitrogen DRAM pools: let 77 K shrink the capacitor
idea: Periodic-table walk, N (7): run rack-scale memory pools at 77 K in LN2 or cryocooled sleds, where access-transistor leakage falls >1e6x and retention rises from 64 ms to hours, so cells can be designed with a 1-1.5 fF capacitor (AR ~15) and no refresh.
why: Deletes the most tool- and material-intensive steps (deep mold etch, high-k stacks) and refresh energy (46 fJ/bit); nitrogen comes from air.

title: DNA-brick crystal hardmasks replace EUV for array layers
idea: Grow 3D DNA-brick crystals with a honeycomb lattice at 24-36 nm pitch on a sparse DUV-printed guide, then mineralize them into a silica or alumina hardmask by sol-gel growth inside the DNA, the way biosilica forms on organic templates. Use it only for the storage-node and bitline-contact array layers, which are purely periodic.
why: Removes 2-3 of the 5-7 EUV layers (single supplier) using sugar-phosphate-nitrogen building blocks; defectivity at wafer scale is the main risk.

title: Self-assembled nanopillar composites multiply capacitor area in one deposition
idea: Ideal: an electrode that sprouts its own forest. Closest: co-sputter a phase-separating film (conductive TiN or NiO-type pillars in an Al2O3/MgO matrix) that spontaneously forms ~5 nm vertical pillars at ~10 nm spacing, etch back the matrix and coat with ALD dielectric and top electrode for 10-30x area gain with no patterning or HAR etch.
why: 100x enabler: gives cheap planar/panel cells pillar-class capacitance for ~$1/m2, deleting capacitor-module masks and fluorocarbon HAR etch on the ~$0.1/GB path. Trades pillar uniformity and tip leakage.

title: Po the fab has no drain: zero-liquid-discharge with fluoride mining
idea: Po: 'the fab has no drain pipe.' Extracted: segregate wastewater by chemistry, reclaim >90% to UPW feed with RO and electrodeionization, crystallize the brine, and precipitate fluoride as acid-grade CaF2 (a fluorspar substitute) and ammonia as fertilizer for sale.
why: Water intensity (net intake falls ~5-10x) and fluorspar (China-dominated) partly offset by recovered fluoride; makes fabs viable in water-stressed U.S. states.

title: Back-grind swarf from HBM thinning recycled into silicon feedstock
idea: TRIZ #22 Blessing in disguise: grinding HBM core dies from 775 um to ~40 um turns ~95% of each wafer (~120 g) into fine swarf. Collect it in a dedicated closed DI loop, strip the oxide shell with HF, and plasma-melt it into silicon feedstock for CZ recharge or solar.
why: Recovers most of the silicon, and its embedded polysilicon energy, from HBM wafers that is landfilled today. HBM uses ~3x the wafer area per bit, so the waste is growing fast.

title: Sourdough baker keeps the starter: porous-silicon wafer printing
idea: Persona: a baker who keeps the starter and bakes many loaves. Anodize a parent wafer into a double-porosity porous-Si layer and grow a 50-100 um DRAM-grade epitaxial film on it. After processing or bonding, split at the weak porous layer and reuse the parent wafer 10-20 times.
why: One crucible-grown wafer yields 10-20 device substrates, so polysilicon, quartz crucibles and crystal-growth energy per bit fall ~5-10x.

title: HBM stacks peel off backside silicon instead of grinding it away
idea: HBM dies are thinned from 775 um to ~30-50 um, which grinds ~95% of every wafer into sludge. A laser-written subsurface damage plane plus polymer-stress cold split, as already used on SiC boules, cleaves off a ~700 um slab that is repolished and reused as monitor, test or epi-base wafers.
why: Recovers ~0.9 wafer of silicon per HBM wafer for the fastest-growing DRAM segment, cutting polysilicon, HPQ crucible demand, grinding water and slurry.

title: Ion-cut layer splitting turns one donor wafer into many device layers
idea: Scale shift from wafer to micrometer layer: existing SOI wafer plants implant hydrogen ~1 um deep, bond to a cheap carrier and split off a single-crystal layer. The donor is re-polished and reused 10-20 times, and DRAM arrays are built on the transferred layers.
why: Cuts high-purity quartz crucible and prime polysilicon intensity ~10x per DRAM wafer using SOI capacity that already exists.

title: Qimonda's trench DRAM revived by metal-assisted chemical etching at 200:1
idea: Trench-capacitor DRAM (IBM, Infineon, Qimonda, IBM eDRAM) died when plasma RIE could not push silicon trenches past ~60-70:1, and Qimonda went bankrupt. Metal-assisted chemical etching sinks a patterned catalyst mesh into silicon in HF/H2O2 vapor with straight walls beyond 200:1; use a sacrificial non-gold catalyst followed by a verified metals strip, then line trenches with ALD TiN/Al2O3-TiO2/TiN.
why: Gives the AR ~115+ needed for >8 fF without high-power C4F8/SF6 plasma (high-GWP, PFAS-class gases); capacitor sits under the transistor so the array stays planar; ~2x capacitance or ~30% smaller cell at the same charge.

title: Vapor-deposited zinc-imidazolate MOF dry resist without fluorinated photoacids
idea: Ideal: a resist made from zinc and a common organic, deposited like a gas. Closest: grow ZIF-8-type zinc 2-methylimidazolate films by vapor-phase MOF-CVD; exposure breaks Zn-N links and the image develops in mild solvent or vapor, with no PFAS photoacid generators, fluorinated surfactants or spin-coat waste.
why: Resist PAGs/surfactants are a top fab PFAS use; dry deposition also cuts resist consumption ~10x and solvent wastewater; zinc is abundant.

title: Zinc-magnesium-oxide ferroelectric tunnel junctions sputtered at room temperature
idea: Effect: polarization-modulated tunnel electroresistance. Wurtzite Zn(1-x)Mg(x)O (x~0.3) is ferroelectric as-deposited at room temperature; a 3-5 nm layer between asymmetric electrodes (TiN / n-ZnO) makes a tunnel junction whose barrier height follows the polarization, so a small read current senses the state without switching it.
why: Hf/Zr-free ferroelectric memory with non-destructive read (fact 8); Zn is abundant and Mg can come from seawater; the process stays near room temperature.

title: Indium-free zinc-tin-oxide gain cell keeps data minutes at 125 C
idea: Magnify bandgap, minify chokepoints: build 2T0C gain cells from amorphous Zn-Sn-O (Eg ~3.3 eV), whose off-current stays below 1e-19 A/um at 125 C, with no indium, no gallium and no high-AR capacitor.
why: Seconds-to-minutes retention at 125 C vs ~32 ms refresh for silicon DRAM above 85 C (fact 3). Removes In/Ga (China-dominated) and the deep capacitor etch; ZTO has no phase change below 300 C.

title: Idle LCD panel fabs print multi-tier oxide memory on glass
idea: Effect: wide-bandgap suppression of intrinsic carrier generation (n_i ~ exp(-Eg/2kT)) gives oxide transistors minutes-long retention even at 1 um rules. Retool idle Gen-8.5 LCD lines, which already run <=350 C oxide TFT processes with i-line litho, to stack 8 tiers of 2T0C gain cells on 5.5 m2 glass, about 0.7 TB per panel.
why: Capital intensity and EUV/fab lead time (3-5 yr): uses existing depreciated panel capacity, no EUV and no CZ wafers; at ~$1.5k/m2 for 8 tiers that is ~$12/GB for a CXL warm tier.

title: Ceria-free iron-oxide Fenton-assisted CMP slurry with magnetic recovery
idea: Periodic-table walk, Fe (26): swap rare-earth ceria abrasives for Fe3O4 nanoparticles plus in-situ Fenton chemistry (Fe2+/H2O2 hydroxyl radicals) that softens oxide surfaces, and recover the magnetic particles from slurry waste with magnets; post-clean in dilute HCl.
why: Removes the CeO2 rare-earth chokepoint and fluorinated surfactants; recycles ~60-80% of abrasive.

title: Hollow-fiber sieving plus pressure swing recaptures fab helium as service
idea: Effect: helium's 2.6 angstrom kinetic diameter lets it permeate polyimide hollow fibers ~100x faster than N2 or Ar. Capture exhaust at chucks, load locks and leak stations, enrich it to 90% through membranes, finish it to 5N by pressure-swing adsorption and refill on site, all sold as helium-as-a-service.
why: Helium chokepoint: 70-90% recovery cuts virgin helium purchases ~5-10x and protects fabs from Qatar-type outages.

title: Supercritical CO2 cleaning, abandoned in 2000s, revived for capacitor rinse-dry
idea: Supercritical CO2 wafer cleaning was abandoned on particle redeposition and slow high-pressure single-wafer chambers. Aim it at the one place it wins: replace the repeated wet clean and IPA dry of 60-75:1 pillars with SC-CO2 plus amine/alcohol cosolvent residue removal and stiction-free drying, recirculating >95% of CO2 captured from ammonia or ethanol plants.
why: Cleaning is a large share of a fab's ultrapure water; claim ~30% water cut on array steps and removal of pattern-collapse yield loss, which also permits taller, thinner pillars.

title: Re-establish the Federal Helium Reserve with mandatory fab helium recapture
idea: Reverse the 2024 sale of the Amarillo Bush Dome reserve: restore a federal helium reserve with semiconductor priority, and revive the 1960 Helium Act's conservation intent by requiring fabs to recapture backside-cooling and leak-test helium with on-site purifiers and liquefiers.
why: Helium chokepoint (Qatar's ~30% offline since March 2026): recapture cuts fab helium purchases 70-90% and the reserve buffers outages.

title: Proton shuttle in phosphosilicate glass: nanosecond nonvolatile resistor
idea: Inverts 'memory state is held by electrons': drive protons under strong short field pulses through a few-nm phosphorus-doped SiO2 electrolyte into and out of a MoO3 or TiO2 channel, changing its conductance 10-100x; the proton stays put without power.
why: Zero refresh; materials are Si, P, O, H and Mo/Ti (abundant, US-available), at BEOL temperatures so it can stack over logic.

title: Crucible liners made from polysilicon plants' silicon tetrachloride waste
idea: Jump from chemical-plant scale to crucible scale: flame-hydrolyze the SiCl4 byproduct of U.S. polysilicon plants into synthetic silica soot. Plasma-fuse it as the 2-3 mm inner crucible layer that touches the melt, backed by ordinary-grade quartz sand.
why: Cuts Spruce Pine high-purity quartz needed per crucible by ~70% using an existing domestic waste stream. Synthetic silica also lowers metal contamination in the ingot.

title: Black-silicon solar etch: catalyst-guided holes reach 100:1 without plasma
idea: Black-silicon solar texturing uses metal-assisted chemical etching (MACE): a patterned Ag film sinks into Si in HF/H2O2 and drills straight holes. Pattern a catalyst mesh by e-beam or nanoimprint in a university fab to drill registered 100:1+ trenches for capacitors or vertical channels, then remove the catalyst with iodide etch plus sacrificial oxidation and verify retention.
why: Plasma-free high-AR etch removes fluorocarbon gases, etch-tool capital and chamber parts and reaches the AR ~115 that fact 1 calls for; metal contamination is the key risk.

title: No working p-type oxide? Build glass memory periphery from n-only circuits
idea: Two decades of p-type oxide TFTs (SnO, Cu2O, NiO) failed to match n-type oxides in mobility or stability, blocking CMOS periphery on glass. Stop chasing p-type: design decoders, wordline drivers and sense amps in n-only pseudo-CMOS with capacitive bootstrapping and precharge-evaluate dynamic logic in the same ZTO layer as the array, sharing 3-4 masks.
why: Periphery is ~49% of a DRAM die; sharing the array's single oxide stack roughly halves mask count on glass and removes the per-tier silicon CMOS chiplet; dynamic-logic power is acceptable at memory duty cycles.
